statements.source_detail: Heard at the pickup counter during the June 12 morning observation

statements.text: If it's more than five minutes I just go to the vending machine.
The drink is great when I finally get it.

needs.text: Get the drink in hand fast enough to make it to class or a meeting -- the whole wait, order to handoff.
The drink is made right the first time -- speed must not cost correctness.

ctqs.measure: Average order-to-handoff time, weekday 7:00-10:00 peak, in minutes
ctqs.critical_vs_easy_check: Customer-critical: S1, S2, and S4 are all about the total wait itself -- customers time their stop against class start. Not chosen for convenience: the POS only stamps order time, so handoff needs a manual tally.

ctqs.measure: Share of peak orders handed off within 5 minutes (%)
ctqs.critical_vs_easy_check: Customer-critical: S4 names five minutes as the walk-away line, so the share past that line matters, not just the average. Harder to measure than the average, not easier -- it needs the same per-order tally.

ctqs.measure: Drink remake rate, remakes per 100 orders
ctqs.target: No worse than the Q2 2026 level (about 3.6 per 100 orders)
ctqs.critical_vs_easy_check: Customer-critical: S5 says the drink itself is why regulars come, so speeding up handoff must not trade away correctness. The waste sheet makes it easy to count, but it earns its place through S5, not through convenience -- it is the charter's guardrail metric.

charter_metric_link: C1 is the charter's primary metric: average order-to-handoff time in minutes, weekday 7:00-10:00 peak -- same operational definition, same direction (lower is better), same target (5.0 minutes by 2026-10-31). C3 appears on the charter as the remake-rate guardrail.
